OpenAPI 3.0 specification

SaveSessionID.name: saveSessionID
SaveSessionID.description: Identifier of an existing save session, matched exactly by SaveEngine. It is never trimmed, normalised or guessed.

CharacterID.name: characterID
CharacterID.description: Physical character slot index 0..9, parsed as a decimal integer. The allowed range is validated by SaveEngine.

OwnedItemID.name: ownedItemID
OwnedItemID.description: Opaque owned-item identity exactly as a previous GetInventory or GetStorage result reported it. It is valid only inside that save session and only while its saveRevision is unchanged. Pass it back unchanged: it is never parsed, trimmed, normalised or reconstructed, and it encodes no handle, no index and no slot address.

ResourceKind.name: kind
ResourceKind.description: schema.Resource.Kind, matched exactly. The kind is resolved before the key. Accepted values: item, colosseum, region, summoning_pool, grace, boss, map_region, tutorial, quest, class.

ResourceKey.name: key
ResourceKey.description: schema.Resource.Key inside the given kind, matched exactly. Its shape depends on the kind: an item key is eight uppercase hexadecimal characters; colosseum, region, summoning pool, grace, boss, map region and quest keys use lowercase letters, digits and underscores; tutorial keys are decimal numbers; class keys are the decimal starting-class ID 0..11. Step keys inside a quest use the historical stable format legacy_NNN. It never carries a kind prefix and is not an Item.GameID, not a variant ID and not a data file name.

RelationType.name: relationType
RelationType.description: schema.RelationKind, matched exactly and case-sensitively. Omitted or empty means every relation type.

RelationDirection.name: direction
RelationDirection.description: Relation direction, matched exactly. Omitted or empty means both directions; there is deliberately no 'both' value. The filtered-out direction stays an empty array.

ResourceTypeFilter.name: resourceType
ResourceTypeFilter.description: schema.Resource.Kind, matched exactly and case-sensitively. Omitted or empty means every kind, which today mixes items, colosseums, regions, summoning pools, graces, bosses, map regions, tutorials, quests and classes in one page.

ItemFamilyFilter.name: family
ItemFamilyFilter.description: schema.ItemFamily, matched exactly and case-sensitively. Omitted or empty means every family. A resource whose family is not known never matches.

CapabilityFilter.name: capability
CapabilityFilter.description: One field of schema.ItemCapabilities. A resource matches only when that capability is both known and enabled, so undecided data never widens the result. Omitted or empty means no capability filter.

EndpointIDFilter.name: endpointId
EndpointIDFilter.description: Not supported. GameCatalog declares no resource-to-endpoint relation, so any non-empty value is rejected with 400 instead of being answered from a guessed mapping. Only the empty value is accepted.

ResourceSearch.name: search
ResourceSearch.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against Resource.Key and the resource name (item name, colosseum name, region name, summoning pool name, grace name, boss name, map region name, tutorial title, or quest name). An unknown name is an empty string and is never searched as a placeholder. Omitted or empty means no search.

ContainerSection.name: containerSection
ContainerSection.description: Physical InventoryHeld section. Omitted or empty means both sections, common means the 0xA80 common records and key means the 0x180 key records. The value is matched exactly and case-sensitively; it is never trimmed and has no alias.

StorageContainerSection.name: containerSection
StorageContainerSection.description: Physical Storage Box section. Omitted or empty means both sections, common means the 0x780 common records and key means the 0x80 key records. The value is matched exactly and case-sensitively; it is never trimmed and has no alias. The two sections are smaller than the InventoryHeld ones, so this parameter is deliberately not the shared containerSection of GetInventory.

AvailabilityFilter.name: availabilityFilter
AvailabilityFilter.description: Unlock-state filter. Omitted or empty means every gesture, unlocked means the unlocked ones only and locked means the rest. The value is matched exactly and case-sensitively; it is never trimmed and has no alias. It can only remove entries and never changes their order.

Page.name: page
Page.description: One-based page number. Omitted, empty or 0 means page 1. A negative value is rejected. A page beyond the last one returns an empty array with the real total.

PageSize.name: pageSize
PageSize.description: Number of entries per page. Omitted, empty or 0 means 50. A negative value is rejected. There is deliberately no maximum.

ValidationScope.name: scope
ValidationScope.description: Restricts the report to one validation scope. It is matched exactly and never trimmed or normalised, so an unknown value is rejected. Omitted or empty means every scope.

DiagnosticLogCursor.name: cursor
DiagnosticLogCursor.description: Exclusive sequence token. Must be a canonical decimal uint64. Omitted or empty reads from the oldest available record.

DiagnosticLogLimit.name: limit
DiagnosticLogLimit.description: Maximum entries to return. Omitted, empty or 0 means 50. Accepted range is 0..200.

DiagnosticLogSeverity.name: severity
DiagnosticLogSeverity.description: Restricts the log to one severity level. Accepted values are "", "info", "warning", "error". In v1, only "info" events are emitted; "warning" and "error" return empty matches.

DiagnosticLogScope.name: scope
DiagnosticLogScope.description: Restricts the log to one diagnostic scope. Accepted values are "", "session", "repairs".

GetRepairPlanRequest.description: The findings to plan for, together with the save revision they were observed at.

saveRevision.description: The revision the findings were observed at, exactly as returned in saveRevision by GetSaveValidationReport. It is required and matched exactly: an issue identifier describes a position inside a report of one revision, so a plan derived from identifiers of an older revision would address findings that have since moved. A revision that no longer matches the session is rejected rather than reinterpreted.

issueIDs.description: The id values of the SaveValidationIssue entries to plan for, from a report of this same character at this same revision. At least one is required. An empty list, a repeated identifier and an identifier naming no current finding are all rejected: the endpoint never guesses which defect a caller meant and never silently returns a smaller plan than was asked for. The order of the request is ignored; the plan is ordered by the report.

ApplyRepairsRequest.description: The selected issue identifiers, the token sealing their executable actions, and the revision the plan was observed at.

issueIDs.description: The exact selected identifiers passed to GetRepairPlan. They let ApplyRepairs derive the candidate actions again; the request order does not matter.

planToken.description: The planToken returned by GetRepairPlan. It must match the freshly derived executable actions exactly.

expectedRevision.description: The exact saveRevision returned by GetRepairPlan. A changed session is rejected rather than reinterpreted.

DiagnosticRecord.description: One safe, structured diagnostic event recorded by SaveEngine.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number of the diagnostic event within the session.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp of the event.

message.description: Fixed human-readable description of the event.

characterID.description: Character slot index (0..9) if the event belongs to a character slot.

revision.description: Save revision associated with the event.

GetDiagnosticLogResult.description: A page of diagnostic records and pagination state.

nextCursor.description: Sequence token to pass as cursor in the next request.

hasMore.description: True if more matching entries exist in the buffer.

totalBuffered.description: Total number of records currently buffered for this session.

cursorExpired.description: True if the requested cursor was overwritten by ring buffer rollover.

oldestAvailableCursor.description: Sequence token of the oldest record currently buffered.

ApplyRepairsResult.description: The result of a fresh, token-verified repair execution. The boolean 'applied' discriminates the two success variants: an executed transaction carries the complete MutationReceipt, and a verified selection without an executable action carries only the session and the unchanged revision. Rejected findings are included for visibility in both variants and never mutate the save.

ApplyRepairsApplied.description: At least one executable action committed, as one atomic mutation of kind apply_repairs.

ApplyRepairsNoAction.description: The freshly derived plan of the selected findings carries no executable action. Nothing was committed, so there is no operationID, no operationKind and no changedScopes, and the revision is the one the request matched.

RepairAction.description: One planned change. It is a description, not an execution: building it changes nothing and reserves nothing.

issueIDs.description: Every finding this one action resolves, in report order. It is a list because the statistics block is repaired by a single atomic set_character_stats over all eight attributes, which can answer several findings at once; a container action always names exactly one. Each requested identifier still points at exactly one action or one rejection, so nothing is ever silently dropped, but an action may be shared.

scope.description: The validation scope the finding was made in.

operation.description: The mutating contract that would carry out this action. The plan never invents a new way to write the save.

ownedItemID.description: The container record the action applies to, valid for the saveRevision of this plan and for nothing else. Absent for an action that names no record.

targetValue.description: The single count the operation sets. Present only for set_owned_item_quantity, which is the one operation whose target is a single number.

attributes.description: The corrected attribute set of a set_character_stats action: the nearest set satisfying both the absolute range 1..99 and the per-attribute minima of the character's own starting class, each attribute moved the smallest legal distance. Absent for every other operation. Applying it also recalculates the stored level from these attributes and raises the lifetime runes to the minimum the levels above the base level of the character's own starting class require, which SetCharacterStats always does.

description.description: Human-readable statement of what the action would change and to what.

RepairRejection.description: One requested finding this build refuses to plan for, with the reason. It exists so a caller never has to read an absent action as either already fine or silently handled: a finding is planned or it is refused, never omitted. A refusal is a result, not an error.

issueID.description: The validation issue that carries no plan.

code.description: The issue code of that finding.

scope.description: The validation scope the finding was made in.

reason.description: Why no repair is derived. Either this build cannot resolve the stored data, so a repair would mean guessing what it was meant to be, or the resolution would need a policy this project has not confirmed.

RepairPlan.description: A non-mutating plan of selected repairs bound to one save version. Actions and rejected together account for every requested identifier exactly once, both ordered by the order the validation report lists their findings, so two plans of the same revision and the same request are identical.

saveSessionID.description: The session the plan was derived from.

saveRevision.description: The save revision the plan is bound to.

characterID.description: The character slot the plan applies to. A plan is per-character because a validation issue identifier is unique inside one slot and nowhere else.

planToken.description: The SHA-256 digest, hex-encoded, of the session identifier, the save revision, the character and every action in order. It is derived rather than random so ApplyRepairs can derive the plan itself, recompute the token and compare: a plan needs no server-side storage, no expiry and no reservation. Any change to the save, the character, the selection or a single action target produces a different token, so a token can never authorise a mutation that was not the one described.

actions.description: The findings whose target state confirmed data determines uniquely.

rejected.description: The requested findings that carry no repair contract, each with the reason. This is deliberately the larger group.

SaveValidationIssue.description: One detected problem. It states what is wrong and where, and deliberately nothing about how to resolve it: this getter proposes no action, no default action and no repair.

id.description: Identifier addressing this one finding for GetRepairPlan. It is derived from the scope, the code and the position of the finding inside its own scope, so it is stable for a given saveRevision and unaffected by the scope filter: a scope is always judged as a whole, so narrowing the report never renumbers what it returns. Like ownedItemID it is valid for the saveRevision of this report and for nothing else.

code.description: Stable identifier of the problem a caller may branch on. The message beside it is not stable.

severity.description: An error names a state the save cannot legally be in. A warning names data this build cannot judge, which is reported rather than silently accepted.

scope.description: The validation scope the problem was found in.

message.description: Human-readable explanation naming the exact rejected field and reason.

ownedItemID.description: Identity of the container record the problem was found in, valid for the saveRevision of this report and for nothing else. Empty for a problem that names no record.

SaveValidationScopeCoverage.description: What one scope actually checked. It exists so an empty issue list can be read correctly: checked false with a reason means the scope could not be decoded and its data was not judged at all, so the save is not thereby clean.

checked.description: True when the scope was decoded and judged.

reason.description: Why the scope was not checked. Empty when it was.

recordsChecked.description: How many records of the scope were judged.

unresolvedRecords.description: How many of those records carried data this build could not resolve, and therefore stayed unjudged.

SaveValidationReport.description: The result of one non-mutating validation pass over a single character slot. Issues are ordered by scope in the order coverage lists them, and inside a scope in the stored order of the data they were found in, so two reports of the same revision are identical. An inactive or residual slot reports active false, no issue and every requested scope unchecked with that reason.

saveRevision.description: The revision the whole report was read under. Every scope describes this one revision.

LoadSaveRequest.description: Body of LoadSave. All three fields reach the endpoint exactly as sent; unknown fields are rejected.

source.description: Path of a local save file. Never trimmed, normalised or defaulted.

expectedPlatform.description: Platform the caller expects. An empty value means the platform is recognised from the container.

sourceKind.description: What the source file is. Required, matched exactly and case-sensitively, with no alias, no empty form and no default: an omitted field is the empty string, which the endpoint rejects without creating a session.

WriteSaveRequest.description: Body of WriteSave. Both fields reach the endpoint exactly as sent; unknown fields are rejected.

expectedRevision.description: Current canonical decimal saveRevision, compared exactly and never normalised.

target.description: Explicit local destination path, passed unchanged and never inferred from LoadSave.

MutationReceipt.description: Shared receipt of one committed save-session mutation. Its five members are flat members of every migrated mutation result; there is no nested receipt object.

operationID.description: Opaque identifier of one concrete execution, never derived from the kind, the revision, an index or a clock. Identifiers do not repeat among the receipts issued by one running SaveEngine instance; that guarantee does not currently cover application restarts, because uniqueness across restarts requires a persistent operation journal and stays outside the receipt migration. A rejected mutation returns none.

operationKind.description: Stable kind of the mutation: exactly the EndpointID of the endpoint that initiated the change.

saveRevision.description: Canonical decimal saveRevision the mutation committed.

changedScopes.description: Backend read scopes this mutation invalidated, in the one canonical order.

WriteSaveResult.description: Receipt of a successful WriteSave. It carries the shared mutation receipt and no domain field of its own.

SetSaveAccountIDRequest.description: Body of SetSaveAccountID. Both fields are required and reach the endpoint exactly as sent; unknown fields are rejected.

accountID.description: Canonical decimal representation of a uint64: 0, or an unsigned number without leading zeros that fits into 64 bits. It is a string because JSON and JavaScript lose the precision of large identifiers.

expectedRevision.description: Current canonical decimal saveRevision, compared exactly and never normalised.

SetSaveAccountIDResult.description: Receipt of a successful SetSaveAccountID. It carries the shared mutation receipt and never the identifier.

CloseSaveResult.description: Confirmation that the named session was removed from memory. The source save file is untouched.

SessionInfo.description: Safe public metadata of a save session. It carries the exact source path and source kind the session was created from and its current save revision, and no SteamID, offset, handle or save byte. The source path is metadata only: the session reads exclusively from its private snapshot and never reopens that file.

sourcePath.description: Exact path the private snapshot was created from, carried verbatim. It is never trimmed, recased, resolved or guessed, and never reopened.

sourceKind.description: What the source file is, echoed back exactly as the caller stated it. 'local' is a durable file the user owns; 'temporary' is a working copy that is not one.

saveRevision.description: Canonical decimal save revision of the session, "0" after LoadSave. A string and not a number, so no consumer can round, increment or reorder it.

unsavedChanges.description: True after a committed in-memory mutation and false after LoadSave or a successful WriteSave.

eventSequence.description: Canonical decimal position of this session's session.changed stream, "0" for a session that has committed nothing. A subscriber reads it to establish or re-establish its baseline after a start, a lost event or a reconnect. A string for the same reason saveRevision is one.

CharacterSummary.description: Summary of one physical character slot. Name and level are reported for an active slot only.

SaveCharacters.description: The session that was read and one summary per physical slot, always ten of them in slot order.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

CharacterProfile.description: Profile of one character slot. startingClassID and gender are raw identifiers and secondsPlayed is a raw second count: none is mapped, formatted or rejected for being unknown.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

CloneCharacterRequest.description: Completely empty target slot and optimistic-concurrency revision for one character clone.

targetSlotID.description: Physical target slot. It must differ from the source and contain only the native empty state.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

CloneCharacterResult.description: Receipt for one committed character clone. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is clone_character.

name.description: Unique name assigned to both stored name copies of the clone.

DeleteCharacterRequest.description: Optimistic-concurrency revision for one permanent character deletion.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

DeleteCharacterResult.description: Receipt for one committed permanent character deletion. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is delete_character.

SetCharacterActiveRequest.description: Target slot activity and optimistic-concurrency revision.

active.description: Target activity state. False preserves residual character bytes; true requires confirmed residual character data when the slot is currently inactive.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterActiveResult.description: Result of one accepted character activity assignment. The boolean 'changed' discriminates the two success variants: a committed mutation carries the complete MutationReceipt, and an idempotent request carries only the session and the unchanged revision.

SetCharacterActiveCommitted.description: The activity flag changed, so a revision was committed and the complete receipt is present.

SetCharacterActiveUnchanged.description: The slot was already in the requested state. Nothing was committed, so there is no operationID, no operationKind and no changedScopes, and the revision is the one the request matched. It is a domain success and not an error.

SetCharacterNameRequest.description: Exact character-name assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision. The name is limited by UTF-16 code units rather than Unicode code points.

name.description: Exact name to store. It must be valid UTF-8, contain no U+0000, and encode to at most 16 UTF-16 code units. No trimming, normalisation, truncation, or character whitelist is applied.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterNameResult.description: Receipt for one committed character-name assignment. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_name.

SetCharacterGenderRequest.description: Body-type assignment through the confirmed default appearance preset and optimistic-concurrency revision.

gender.description: Target body type: 0 applies the Type B Ciri default; 1 applies the Type A Geralt default.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterGenderResult.description: Receipt for one body-type change through its complete default appearance preset. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_gender and never set_character_appearance, although both share one SaveEngine writer.

CharacterUndoState.description: The undo state of one character slot in one save session.

saveRevision.description: The session's current canonical decimal revision.

available.description: True only when the session's single undo point belongs to this character and to the current revision.

undoToken.description: Opaque identifier of the available undo point. Absent when available is false. It is not a GameResource reference.

operationKind.description: Stable kind of the mutation the undo point would revert, equal to the EndpointID of the endpoint that performed it, such as set_character_stats. Absent when available is false.

UndoCharacterChangesRequest.description: The undo point to consume and the optimistic-concurrency revision.

undoToken.description: The exact token reported by GetUndoState for this character. It is matched byte for byte.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

UndoCharacterChangesResult.description: Receipt for one consumed undo point. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is undo_character_changes, while undoneOperationKind names the reverted mutation and changedScopes are that mutation's scopes. saveRevision is the revision created by the undo, exactly one above the revision the request matched.

undoneOperationKind.description: Stable kind of the mutation that was reverted, equal to the EndpointID of the endpoint that performed it.

SetCharacterRunesRequest.description: Exact held-runes assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision.

runes.description: Exact held-runes value to store. Values outside the legal range are rejected, never clamped.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterRunesResult.description: Receipt for one committed held-runes assignment. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_runes.

CharacterAttributes.description: The complete writable attribute set. All eight fields are mandatory; an omitted field is rejected, never read as zero.

SetCharacterStatsRequest.description: Complete attribute assignment, level policy and optimistic-concurrency revision. The level is not an input.

levelPolicy.description: Accepted exactly as written. The value is never trimmed or normalised, and no other policy exists.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterStatsResult.description: Receipt for one committed statistics assignment. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_stats. It reports the accepted attributes and the two values SaveEngine derived from them.

SetCharacterStartingClassRequest.description: Starting class assignment, the explicit confirmation of the destructive build reset it performs, and the optimistic-concurrency revision.

startingClassID.description: Target starting class identifier (0..11). Regulation 1.17 added 10 Idus Knight and 11 Heavy Knight to the ten base classes.

confirmReset.description: Explicit confirmation that all eight attributes and the Rune Level may be reset to the base values of the target class. Only true performs the mutation; false or an omitted field is rejected and leaves the save and its revision unchanged.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterStartingClassResult.description: Receipt for one committed starting-class mutation. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_starting_class. Reports the base attributes and the base Rune Level of the applied class together with the SoulMemory the mutation left unchanged.

soulMemory.description: Lifetime runes (TotalGetSoul) exactly as stored. This mutation never changes them.

CharacterStats.description: Raw statistics stored in one character slot. Every number is the value stored in the save: nothing is validated, normalised, clamped or computed.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

CharacterAppearance.description: Raw appearance stored in one character slot. Every number is the value stored in the save: nothing is validated, normalised, clamped, computed or resolved to a name. An inactive slot reports active false and zero values.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

modelIDs.description: The eight raw model identifiers, in stored order.

faceShape.description: The raw face shape parameter block, one number per stored byte.

body.description: The raw body parameter block, one number per stored byte.

skin.description: The raw skin parameter block, one number per stored byte.

CharacterAppearanceValues.description: Complete writable raw appearance model. Model identifiers retain their full uint32 values; the other arrays contain raw save bytes.

SetCharacterAppearanceRequest.description: Complete raw appearance assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetCharacterAppearanceResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete appearance assignment. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_character_appearance and never the kind of another entry point of the same SaveEngine appearance writer.

presetID.description: Exact, case-sensitive appearance preset ID from GameCatalog.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

ApplyAppearancePresetResult.description: Receipt for one appearance preset applied through the complete appearance mutation. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is apply_appearance_preset and never set_character_appearance, although both share one SaveEngine writer.

CharacterEquipment.description: Raw 22-slot ChrAsmEquipment state of one character slot. Every number is the value stored in the save: nothing is normalised, masked, turned into a handle, stripped of its type bits or resolved against GameCatalog. An inactive slot reports active false and an all-zero slots array.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

slots.description: The 22 raw equipment fields, in stored order. The meaning of each index is documented in docs/endpoints/equipment/get_equipment.md; the values are returned without any normalisation.

LoadoutSlotState.description: Public state of one loadout position. Locked is currently used only for unavailable talisman positions.

LoadoutSlot.description: One positional equipment or Physick slot. Resource presentation is present only when the position is occupied.

LoadoutOwnedSlot.description: One Quick Items or Pouch position. An occupied position carries the revision-scoped ownedItemID and current quantity of the referenced Inventory row.

LoadoutSpellSlot.description: One public playable spell position. Memory Slots and resource presentation are present only when occupied.

CharacterLoadout.description: One revisioned, coherent and catalog-resolved character loadout. An inactive slot returns empty group arrays and no residual slot data.

SetEquippedArmamentsRequest.description: Complete six-position hand-armament assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision.

slotAssignments.description: Exactly six positions in left 1, right 1, left 2, right 2, left 3 and right 3 order. Each position is null to select the native Unarmed record, or an ownedItemID string for a positive Inventory common weapon record.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetEquippedArmamentsResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete hand-armament assignment, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_equipped_armaments.

EquippedArmamentAssignment.description: Canonical catalog identity plus the exact materialized weapon game ID, which preserves upgrade and infusion variants.

SetEquippedArmorRequest.description: Complete four-position armor assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision.

slotAssignments.description: Exactly four positions in head, chest, arms and legs order. Each position is null to select the native bare-body record, or an ownedItemID string for a positive Inventory common armor record.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetEquippedArmorResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete armor assignment, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_equipped_armor.

QuickItemSlot.description: One raw Quick Items record exactly as stored: the item field followed by the equip-index field, both little-endian uint32. Neither value is normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog.

CharacterQuickItems.description: Raw Quick Items state of one character slot: the ten EquipItemData records in stored order and the raw active-slot value behind them. Nothing is normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog. An inactive slot reports active false, ten zeroed records and activeQuick 0.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

items.description: The ten raw Quick Items records, in stored order. The values are returned without any normalisation.

activeQuick.description: The raw active-slot value stored behind the ten records. It keeps its sign: a negative value is reported as written.

PouchItemSlot.description: One raw Pouch record exactly as stored: the item field followed by the equip-index field, both little-endian uint32. Neither value is normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog.

CharacterPouchItems.description: Raw Pouch state of one character slot: the six EquipItemData records that follow the ten Quick Items records and the active-slot value, in stored order. Nothing is normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog. An inactive slot reports active false and six zeroed records.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

items.description: The six raw Pouch records, in stored order. The values are returned without any normalisation.

CharacterPhysickMixture.description: Raw Flask of Wondrous Physick mixture of one character slot: the two Crystal Tear identifiers at the start of EquipPhysicsData, in stored order. Nothing is normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog. An inactive slot reports active false and two zeros.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

tears.description: The two raw Crystal Tear identifiers, in stored order. The values are returned without any normalisation.

SetPhysickMixtureRequest.description: Complete two-position Physick assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision. A null array entry clears that exact position.

crystalTearResources.description: Exactly two positions in stored order. Each non-null ResourceRef must resolve to an owned Crystal Tear; null is the native empty position.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetPhysickMixtureResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete Physick assignment, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_physick_mixture.

SetQuickItemsRequest.description: Complete ten-position Quick Items assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision. A null array entry clears that exact position.

slotAssignments.description: Exactly ten positions in stored order. Each position is null to clear the slot, or a public ownedItemID string pointing to an active common Inventory record.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetQuickItemsResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete Quick Items assignment, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_quick_items.

SetPouchItemsRequest.description: Complete six-position Pouch assignment and optimistic-concurrency revision. A null array entry clears that exact position.

slotAssignments.description: Exactly six positions in stored order. Each position is null to clear the slot, or a public ownedItemID string pointing to an active Inventory record.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetPouchItemsResult.description: Receipt for one committed complete Pouch assignment, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_pouch_items.

SetEquippedSpellsRequest.description: Compact list of spell resources and optimistic-concurrency revision.

orderedResources.description: At most 12 spell resources in desired memory slot order.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetEquippedSpellsResult.description: Receipt for one committed equipped-spells update, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_equipped_spells.

SetEquippedTalismansRequest.description: Compact ordered list of owned talisman instances and optimistic-concurrency revision.

orderedOwnedItemIDs.description: At most four ownedItemID tokens in desired talisman-slot order. The list must also fit the character's unlocked slot count.

expectedRevision.description: Canonical decimal revision that must equal the session's current revision.

SetEquippedTalismansResult.description: Receipt for one committed talisman loadout, expressed with public catalog identities. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_equipped_talismans.

EquippedSpellSlot.description: One physical EquippedSpells record: the raw MagicParam ID exactly as stored, and the GameCatalog resource key, name and Memory Slots cost of the spell it resolves to. The three resolved fields are empty or zero only for the native empty record, whose raw identifier is the sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF.

CharacterEquippedSpells.description: Equipped spells of one character slot: the twelve public playable EquippedSpells records in stored order, the Memory Slots the occupied records consume, and the Memory Slots the character may fill. An inactive slot reports active false, twelve zero-value records and both counts zero.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

spells.description: The twelve public playable spell records, in stored order. The raw MagicParam identifier of every record is returned without any normalisation.

usedMemorySlots.description: Sum of the Memory Slots costs GameCatalog states for the occupied records.

availableMemorySlots.description: Memory Slots the character may fill: the base capacity plus the effective Memory Stones, capped by the game maximum, plus the Moon of Nokstella bonus while that talisman sits in an unlocked talisman field.

InventoryRecord.description: One non-empty physical InventoryHeld record, its opaque owned-item identity and its resolved ItemDocument identity. kind and key are the canonical catalog resource reference; gameID is the exact catalog game ID resolved from the save and selects a materialised variant where applicable. containerSection and physicalIndex identify the physical row it currently occupies and are deliberately not an item identity, because a row moves when the game rewrites the section. gaItemHandle and acquisitionIndex are raw stored values, while quantity has its high bit removed by the 0x7FFFFFFF mask.

ownedItemID.description: Opaque identity of this physical record, valid only for the saveRevision of the enclosing result and only inside the save session that produced it. Compare it byte for byte; never parse, trim, normalise or persist it. It encodes no handle, no index and no slot address, and an Inventory record never shares it with a Storage record at the same coordinates.

kind.description: The GameCatalog resource kind of the resolved item.

key.description: The canonical GameCatalog resource key of the resolved item.

gameID.description: The exact GameCatalog game ID resolved from the save. It selects an item variant where applicable.

containerSection.description: The physical section the record was read from.

physicalIndex.description: Position of the record inside its own section, counted from 0.

gaItemHandle.description: The raw stored GaItem handle. It is not normalised, validated or resolved against GameCatalog.

quantity.description: The stored quantity with the high bit masked off, because that bit is not part of the count.

CharacterInventory.description: One page of resolved InventoryHeld records of one character slot. Every active record carries an ItemDocument kind, canonical key and exact resolved gameID; the remaining physical fields and paging rules are preserved. An inactive or residual slot reports active false, total 0 and an empty array, mints no identity, and still reports the current saveRevision.

saveRevision.description: The revision this result was read under, and the one every ownedItemID in it was minted under. A non-empty decimal string with no sign, prefix, padding or separator. It is deliberately not a JSON number, because a uint64 above 2^53-1 would round in a JavaScript client. Carry it back unchanged as expectedRevision and compare it byte for byte; never parse, increment or order it.

records.description: The requested page in physical native order, the common section first and then the key section. Empty, never null, when the slot is inactive or the page lies beyond the last one.

total.description: Number of non-empty records that passed the section filter, counted before paging.

page.description: The effective one-based page, so a requested 0 is reported as 1.

pageSize.description: The effective page size, so a requested 0 is reported as 50.

CookbookEntry.description: One cookbook GameCatalog declares, together with whether the character has unlocked it. kind and key are the public GameCatalog identity of the goods ItemDocument that declares the single item.unlocks entry of kind cookbook; that identity is unique across a result. The event flag identifier behind the state stays internal, and no provenance, source record, offset or raw save byte is exposed.

kind.description: The GameCatalog resource kind. Always item for a cookbook.

key.description: The GameCatalog resource key of the declaring ItemDocument. One resource declares exactly one cookbook, so the key never repeats in a result.

name.description: The cookbook name stored in the unlock entry. Never empty; a missing name is a fail-closed error.

category.description: The cookbook series stored in the unlock entry. Never empty; a missing category is a fail-closed error.

unlocked.description: True when the event flag of this cookbook is set in the requested slot.

GetCookbooksResult.description: The cookbooks of one character slot that passed availabilityFilter, ordered by category, then name, then the key of the declaring resource. The order never depends on the unlock state. An inactive or residual slot reports active false and every cookbook locked, and its event flags are never read.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

active.description: True only when the slot's activity flag is exactly 1.

cookbooks.description: The cookbooks that passed availabilityFilter, in the deterministic order. Empty, never null.

BellBearingEntry.description: One goods ItemDocument that declares exactly one bell_bearing unlock, together with its acquisition state. The raw event flag is not exposed.

unlocked.description: True when the Bell Bearing acquisition flag is set.

GetBellBearingsResult.description: The Bell Bearings of one character slot that passed availabilityFilter, ordered by category, name and key. The array is empty rather than null.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

SetBellBearingUnlockedRequest.description: The request body for setting a Bell Bearing handed-in state.

bellBearingKey.description: The public 8-digit hex resource key of the Bell Bearing.

unlocked.description: True to mark the Bell Bearing as handed in and consume matching records; false to clear only the acquisition flag.

expectedRevision.description: The canonical decimal save revision string expected by the caller.

SetBellBearingUnlockedResult.description: The receipt returned after a successful Bell Bearing handed-in state mutation. The shared mutation receipt is composed flat: operationKind is set_bell_bearing_unlocked.

ColosseumEntry.description: One colosseum ColosseumDocument reduced to its public identity together with its logical unlock state. The entry carries no unlock event flag; the full document does.

unlocked.description: True when the declared unlock event flag is set in the character slot.

GetColosseumsResult.description: The colosseums of one character slot, ordered by name and then key. The array is empty rather than null.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

RegionEntry.description: One curated RegionDocument reduced to its public identity and its exact membership state in UnlockedRegions. The raw region ID stays private.

unlocked.description: True when the internal region ID is present in the character's UnlockedRegions list.

GetRegionsResult.description: The curated regions of one character slot, ordered by area, name and key. The array is empty rather than null.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

SummoningPoolEntry.description: One curated SummoningPoolDocument reduced to its public identity, its curated region label and its activation state. The raw activation event flag ID stays private.

regionLabel.description: Curated presentation and grouping label. It is not a resource reference and never resolves to a RegionDocument.

activated.description: True when the activation event flag of the pool is set in the character slot.

GetSummoningPoolsResult.description: The curated summoning pools of one character slot, ordered by regionLabel, name and key. The array is empty rather than null.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

GraceEntry.description: One curated GraceDocument reduced to its public identity, its curated region label, its boss-arena fact, its dungeon type and its visit state. The raw visit and door event flag IDs stay private.

regionLabel.description: Curated presentation and grouping label. It is not a resource reference and never resolves to a RegionDocument.

bossArena.description: True when the curated table records the grace as a boss-arena grace.

dungeonType.description: The confirmed sealed-entrance dungeon family of the grace. Empty is the confirmed value of a grace that is behind no such entrance.

visited.description: True when the visit event flag of the grace is set in the character slot.

GetGracesResult.description: The curated Sites of Grace of one character slot, ordered by regionLabel, name and key. The array is empty rather than null.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

BossEntry.description: One curated BossDocument reduced to its public identity, its curated region label, its encounter type, its remembrance fact and its defeat state. The raw defeat event flag ID stays private.

regionLabel.description: Curated presentation and grouping label. It is not a resource reference and never resolves to a RegionDocument.

encounterType.description: The confirmed encounter type of the curated table: main or field.

remembrance.description: True when the curated table records the boss as dropping a Remembrance item.

FieldError.description: One rejected request field. It carries the field, a stable code and a safe English fallback, and nothing else.

AppError.description: The shared public error model. A consumer classifies a failure by code and never by the wording of message; message is a safe English fallback for a code the client does not know. A raw Go error, a stack trace, a private path and an unredacted parameter are never part of it: the cause stays in the backend log beside the same diagnosticID.

message.description: Safe English fallback. The final user-facing text belongs to the frontend.

params.description: Safe parameters of the message, keyed by name.

currentRevision.description: The session's current saveRevision. Present only on revision_conflict, which mutates nothing and is never retried automatically.

diagnosticID.description: Unpredictable identifier correlating this response with the backend log entry that holds the private cause.

Error.description: Error envelope of every route. Its single member is the shared public error model.

SupportedSchema.description: One schema the backend can read and the version range it accepts for it.

applicationVersion.description: Returned exactly as supplied by the backend caller.

valid.description: True only means schema.ValidateManifest accepted the manifest.

Resource.description: schema.Resource identified by the (kind, key) pair. It is a union over the resource kinds: kind 'item' carries ItemDocument, kind 'colosseum' carries ColosseumDocument, kind 'region' carries RegionDocument, kind 'summoning_pool' carries SummoningPoolDocument, kind 'grace' carries GraceDocument, kind 'boss' carries BossDocument, kind 'map_region' carries MapRegionDocument, kind 'tutorial' carries TutorialDocument, kind 'quest' carries QuestDocument and kind 'class' carries ClassDocument. Documents of other kinds are absent, never null. The documents are passed through as stored in the catalog; the full shape of ItemDocument is owned by the catalog schema, not by this explorer.

item.description: The complete schema.ItemDocument as stored, with presentation, capabilities, safety, storage, acquisition, modifiers, links, variants, aliases, unlocks, related technical records, source records, the family block and full provenance. Present exactly when kind is 'item'.

ColosseumDocument.description: schema.ColosseumDocument. The arena name and the unlock event flag come from different sources, so each is a separate fact with its own provenance and neither is derived from the other.

name.description: schema.Fact[string] holding the arena name the game itself shows.

unlockEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the event flag whose set bit records the unlock in a save. GetColosseums does not report it; the full document does.

RegionDocument.description: schema.RegionDocument. Region ID, name and area are separate known facts with provenance from the curated invasion and blue-summon allowlist.

regionID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the internal PlayRegionParam row ID stored in UnlockedRegions.

SummoningPoolDocument.description: schema.SummoningPoolDocument. Name, region label and activation event flag ID are separate known facts with provenance from the curated Martyr Effigy table. The region label is a presentation and grouping label only and is never a resource reference.

activationEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the activation event flag of the pool, confirmed to lie inside block 670.

GraceDocument.description: schema.GraceDocument. Name, region label, visit event flag ID, boss-arena fact, dungeon type and door event flag ID are separate known facts with provenance from the curated Site of Grace table. The region label is a presentation and grouping label only and is never a resource reference. The door event flag is private catalog data no getter exposes; zero is its confirmed value for a grace with no dependent door.

visitEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the visit event flag of the grace, confirmed to lie inside one of the blocks 71, 72, 73, 74 or 76.

doorEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the overworld ObjAct flag that opens the sealed dungeon entrance. Zero means the grace has no dependent door.

BossDocument.description: schema.BossDocument. Name, region label, encounter type, remembrance fact and defeat event flag ID are separate known facts with provenance from the curated synchronized boss defeat table. The region label is a presentation and grouping label only and is never a resource reference. The defeat event flag is private catalog data no getter exposes.

defeatEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the synchronized defeat event flag of the boss, confirmed to lie inside block 9 alone. The neighbouring blocks 8 and 10 carry no curated boss and are not part of the contract.

MapRegionDocument.description: schema.MapRegionDocument. Name, area label and visibility event flag ID are separate known facts with provenance from the curated safe MapVisible table. The area label is only a presentation and grouping label. System display switches, unsafe sub-region flags and transient pickup flags are absent.

visibleEventFlagID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding a safe map visibility event flag, confirmed to lie inside block 62 alone.

TutorialDocument.description: schema.TutorialDocument. The TutorialParam row ID stored in TutorialData and the official English TutorialTitle are separate known facts with independent provenance.

tutorialID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the TutorialParam row ID used as the resource key and stored in TutorialData after unlock.

title.description: schema.Fact[string] holding the official non-empty TutorialTitle FMG value.

ClassDocument.description: schema.ClassDocument. The starting class ID, official English class name, base Rune Level and eight base attributes are separate known facts with independent provenance.

startingClassID.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class ID stored in PlayerGameData.

name.description: schema.Fact[string] holding the official non-empty class name from GR_MenuText FMG.

level.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the base Rune Level of the class, taken directly from the CharaInitParam soulLv field and never derived from the attribute sum.

vigor.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Vigor.

mind.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Mind.

endurance.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Endurance.

strength.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Strength.

dexterity.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Dexterity.

intelligence.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Intelligence.

faith.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Faith.

arcane.description: schema.Fact[uint32] holding the starting-class base Arcane.

QuestFlag.description: schema.QuestFlag. An event flag state assignment within a quest step.

QuestStepDocument.description: schema.QuestStepDocument. One supported step of an NPC questline.

QuestDocument.description: schema.QuestDocument. An NPC questline declaring supported steps with canonical event flag plans.

ItemVariant.description: schema.ItemVariant as stored in the catalog, with full provenance.

ResourceRef.description: schema.ResourceRef: the (kind, key) pair that identifies a resource. There is no numeric resource identifier.

Relation.description: schema.Relation as derived and stored by the catalog. Both endpoints are ResourceRef objects, never numeric IDs.

provenance.description: The evidence the catalog derived the relation from.

ResourceListEntry.description: Picker-sized projection of one resource. Relations, variants, provenance, capabilities and the full item document are deliberately absent; they belong to GetResource, GetResourceRelations and GetItemVariants.

family.description: Empty when the resource carries no item document or its family is not known.

name.description: The item, colosseum, region, summoning pool, grace, boss or map region name. Empty when the name is not known; there is no fallback to the key or to a placeholder.

resources.description: The requested page in catalog order, kind first and only then key. Empty, never null, when the page lies beyond the last one.

total.description: Number of resources that passed the filters, counted before paging.

page.description: The effective one-based page, so a requested 0 is reported as 1.

pageSize.description: The effective page size, so a requested 0 is reported as 50.

ResourcePresentationIdentity.description: One exact GameCatalog identity. Neither field is trimmed, normalised, recased or matched through an alias.

ResourcePresentationSummary.description: Scalar-only presentation metadata for one exact resource. Unknown name and iconPath facts are encoded as empty strings; no fallback or placeholder is invented.

iconPath.description: Validated embedded GameCatalog path, or empty when the resource has no known icon.

identities.description: Ordered identities to resolve. Duplicates are preserved. An empty or omitted array is valid.

resources.description: Presentation summaries in the exact input order, including duplicates. Empty, never null, for an empty request.

NetworkParamValues.description: The tunable PvP/multiplayer parameters grouped by player role. The field set and JSON names are owned by GameCatalog.

NetworkPreset.description: One backend preset: its stable identifier and the full parameter values it stands for.

presets.description: Every backend preset in backend order, or exactly the one requested preset. Never null.

GetNetworkSettingsResult.description: The network parameters stored in one save session. The parameter model is the same NetworkParamValues the presets use, so a stored set and a preset set are directly comparable; the endpoint itself compares nothing.

saveRevision.description: Opaque revision of the save session snapshot returned by this read.

SetNetworkSettingsResult.description: Receipt of one committed complete network-parameter assignment, with the committed values.

ApplyNetworkPresetResult.description: Receipt of one committed network preset. operationKind is apply_network_preset and never set_network_settings, although both endpoints share one SaveEngine writer.

AppearancePresetSummary.description: List metadata of one appearance preset. The full appearance configuration (voice type, model identifiers, faceShape, body and skin) stays inside GameCatalog and is not returned by this getter.

id.description: Stable lowercase kebab-case identifier. It equals the image file name without the .jpg suffix.

image.description: Asset file name inside backend/gamecatalog/data/assets/appearance. No route serves the image yet.

bodyType.description: Public label of the stored numeric body type: 1 is Type A, 0 is Type B.

tags.description: Tags of the preset. Never null; empty for every stored preset today.

presets.description: The matching preset summaries in the order of presets/appearance.json. Never null; empty when nothing matches.

name.description: User-facing display name of the template

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp in RFC3339 format

inventoryItems.description: Count of inventory items in this template

storageItems.description: Count of storage items in this template

warnings.description: Count of warnings associated with this template

templateRevision.description: Opaque generation token of the library entry, the canonical decimal form of the persistent per-template revision counter. An entry written before the counter existed reports "0".

templates.description: Matching template metadata entries in UpdatedAt descending order. Never null; empty when no templates match.

total.description: Total number of templates matching the filters before paging

templateRevision.description: Opaque generation token of the library entry, the canonical decimal form of the persistent per-template revision counter. It is not part of the portable template document. An entry written before the counter existed reports "0".
The templateRevision the caller last read for this template, echoed back unchanged. It must be the canonical decimal token; "0" is the token of an entry written before the revision counter existed.

templateID.description: Identifier of the template that was removed from the library

saveSessionID.description: Identifier of the loaded save session

selection.description: Explicit data selection. Supported sections and fields for template creation: 'profile' (fields 'name' and 'level' only; boolean shortcut is rejected), 'stats' (all eight attributes or boolean true), and 'spells' (fields 'spell1'..'spell12' only; boolean shortcut is rejected). Sections 'equipment', 'inventory.workspace', 'items', 'inventoryLayout', and 'storageLayout' are rejected.
